tool_analysis:
Step Analysis:
- The recorded session navigates to a WordPress post, clicks a comment's 'Reply' link (which sets replytocom=<id>#respond), fills the comment form fields (comment, author, email), and submits the form. After submission the page shows the new reply under the target comment.

Task Definition:
- Single purpose: Post a reply to a specific comment on a WordPress-style post page by setting reply context, filling required fields, submitting, and confirming the result.

Action Plan:
1) Navigate to the post URL with replytocom={comment_parent} and fragment #respond to open the reply form and set the hidden comment_parent. 2) Wait briefly for the form to become visible. 3) Fill textarea#comment with the reply text. 4) Fill input#author and input#email with provided values. 5) Click the submit control to post the reply. 6) Wait for response and extract page content to verify the reply or capture errors.

Variable Identification (inputs):
- post_url (required): the post page URL (used as navigation base).
- comment_parent (required): the numeric comment id to reply to (used as replytocom and to verify hidden comment_parent). 
- comment (required): reply body (maps to textarea#comment). 
- author (required): name field.
- email (required): email field (format validated by caller). 
- wait_seconds (optional): time to wait after submit; default used if not provided.

Step Optimization:
- Replaced the UI click on the 'Reply' link with a deterministic navigation that appends replytocom and anchors to #respond; this is more reliable and faster than clicking dynamically-generated links. 
- Used recorded element hashes for the comment textarea, author input, email input, and submit control (elementHash values: textarea=67f1dce8d0, author=085915c9f4, email=cedb6c9f0b, submit=777443c52e) to make interactions deterministic.
- Omitted non-essential interactions (website field and cookie checkbox) because they are optional; the core required fields (comment, author, email) are included and marked required per observed page labels.

Assumptions and Notes:
- The agent is already authenticated if the site requires it; no login steps are included. 
- The post uses a standard WordPress comment form with textarea#comment, input#author, input#email and a submit control accessible by the recorded element hashes. 
- If the host uses different element IDs or the DOM changes, the elementHash-based steps may need updating. The navigation step ensures the reply context is set by using replytocom and #respond rather than relying on click ordering.
name: reply_to_comment_on_wp_post
description: Automate replying to a WordPress-style comment on a post page. The tool navigates to the post URL with a replytocom parameter to set reply context, fills the comment, name and email fields, clicks the submit control, waits, and extracts the page to verify the reply or capture errors. Uses deterministic element hashes recorded during the session for inputs and submit click.

steps.description: Navigate to the post URL with replytocom set to the target comment and anchor the page to the reply form (#respond) to set reply context.
Allow the page to update and the reply context (#respond) to become visible.
Enter the reply text into the comment textarea (textarea#comment).
Enter the commenter's name into the author input (input#author).
Enter the commenter's email into the email input (input#email).
Click the comment form submit control (input#submit or button[type=submit]) to post the reply.
Wait for the server to process the submission and the page to update (default wait).
Capture page content to verify success or get error details.
steps.goal: Confirm the reply was posted under comment id {comment_parent} (look for the posted text and author), or capture any error/server messages displayed after submission.

input_schema.name: post_url
input_schema.description: Canonical post URL where the comment thread lives (e.g. "http://localhost:8000/?p=8").

input_schema.name: comment_parent
input_schema.description: Numeric id of the comment to reply to (used as replytocom and comment_parent, e.g. "15").

input_schema.name: comment
input_schema.description: Reply text to post in the comment textarea (maps to textarea#comment).

input_schema.name: author
input_schema.description: Name to post with the reply (maps to input#author).

input_schema.name: email
input_schema.description: Email to post with the reply (maps to input#email).

input_schema.name: wait_seconds
input_schema.description: Seconds to wait after submitting before verification. Default: 2.
